subject: discrepancy between sampled posteriors and underlying true parameters in a reinforced poisson proces

messages.subject: discrepancy between sampled posteriors and underlying true parameters in a reinforced poisson proces
parts:
Hello!
I am building a model of citation dynamics of the law based on http://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0778, which proposes a reinforced poisson process. To test my model, I generated data according to that stochastic process. My data thus consists of 1000 vectors of variable length, each representing the attentions received by a putative document. I fixed all the parameters except for the "intrinsic importance" parameter lambda. This parameter I drew from a Gamma(1.2,scale=0.8) distribution. I also randomly drew T, the end of the observation period, which is an observed quantity that enters the model. The model as well as my stan code are in the attachment. 
I am having some difficulty interpreting the discrepancy between the lambda values I drew when I generated the data and the posterior samples I obtain. The attached png figure shows that in general the estimated lambdas don't have as large a spread and do not give a 1-1 linear relationship with my original lambdas. The original data include some high values for the lambdas but the draws from the posteriors of those high value lambdas are much smaller. The only draws showing high lambdas are for short vectors (usually associated with smaller lambdas since lambda influences how many citations a document will attract) because of the large uncertainty.
Since I eventually need to also estimate the other parameters and the hyper-parameters (the parameters of the gamma), I am quite worried to see that even this first step gives me unreliable inferences. I would appreciate any ideas regarding where things might be going wrong. I am happy to provide the code by which I generated the data in the first place. 
Thank you for your help!
Marion
